# Project Premise

	The idea is that you play as a paranormal investigation agency, with the joke being that none of the characters have any clue what they are doing. Random fun characters, desperate for a job, sign up with you, thinking that you’re the head of an elaborate shadowy government organization with vast expertise and resources. In truth, that organization was destroyed by paranormal threats and disorganized, untrained subcontractors are all that are left. 

You meet applicants in coffee shops because there is no office. “HQ” is just you in your car with a laptop. When the investigators expose vast paranormal threats, they think they can call in the cavalry to deal with it. But there is no calvary. Just them. So in typical roguelike fashion, the players are expected to die a lot. But by overcoming extreme difficulty, the rag-tag group of amateurs and misfits can heroically overcome apocalyptic threats, as is typical of paranormal adventure stories.

# Gameplay Mechanics

	The game is played out similar to a group-based turned-based time management game. Although the premise is completely different, the closest comparison mechanically is probably the obscure Chinese game “Sultan’s Game.” Other games like “Dead in Antares”, “Dead in Vinland”, and “Dead in Bermuda,” or “The Long Dark” and “I Was a Teenaged Exocolonist” have some similarity. “Cultist Simulator” is also a comparable game, and has a somewhat similar tone to Top Expert (except less sardonic.)  
The player’s main resource is their team of investigators.  Each turn, they can slot their investigators on ever-evolving opportunities on the board, to have that investigator try and utilize that opportunity that turn. The opportunity might be open to any investigator, or might have prerequisite (like a task that can only be performed by an investigator with psychic powers.) The opportunity might complete automatically, or might require a skill check. The opportunity might advance the case, opening up new opportunities on the board. It also might yield helpful cards, like equipment or insights that can be used to help pass skill checks. Failing a skill check might hurt investigators, consume resources, or just waste time.  
The player also has their inventory of helpful cards. Some slots in the board don’t need an investigator and just need an appropriate item. For example, if the rent is due, the player needs to slot in enough money into the “Pay rent” opportunity before the turn timer expires, or else they’ll lose access to whatever they were paying rent on.  
Each investigator has various skills. These skills can grow over the course of the game. Certain events can also grant investigators special new skills. The skill growth, combined with the accumulation of helpful items, allows the player to overcome the game’s escalating difficulty and ultimately win the game.  
In typical roguelike fashion, the players are expect to die and restart a lot. The cases are randomly selected each session, though hard cases unlock late in the game and easy cases are only available in the early game.

# Cases

	Each case should have the feel of a classic paranormal story. Whether it’s from a “Goosebumps” novel, and “Steven King” novel, an “X-Files” episode, or any other source, the common theme is: take an every day relatable experience, like camping or getting a dog or attending marching band practice. Then give it some fun/interesting supernatural twist. “Top Expert” deviates a little from the norm in that the cases are generally supposed to be sardonic in tone. The idea isn’t to play everything super straight like in Lovecraft Horror. The idea is to put under-trained, under-paid entry-level employees in ridiculous situations, which they tolerate because they assume this is all just part of their job. They assume they’re part of an organization that has everything under control, when in truth absolutely nothing is under control, and they’re facing profound mortal peril for 50% above minimum wage and no healthcare.

# Endings Concepts

- Learn the truth and die  
  - Discover some threat so apocalyptic that you have to call in the real experts. Then learn there are no real experts, and die  
- Become true top expert, founding the organization you thought was employing you  
  - Requires discovering some threat so apocalyptic that you have to call in the real experts, then become the real experts, and save the day  
  - Depending on how you handle the threat, you can create different organizations  
    - An organization that is overtly corrupt and backed by sinister forces  
    - An organization that trying to be above-board and uncorrupt if possible  
- Rule the town/ world  
  - You utilize evil cults, powerful artifacts, and make deals with dark gods to seize power  
  - The real top experts never come, but you have to deal with other dark gods  
- Destroy the world  
  - Let none survive  
  - Maybe serve a particular evil god dedicated to annihilation successfully  
- Fix reality  
  - You harness cosmic forces to eliminate all paranormality, rendering yourself jobless  
- Take the money and run  
  - You make enough money to retire early  
- Bad but interesting endings  
  - Trapped forever in a time loop  
  - Turned into a little dog but you’re happy as a little dog  
  - Return the world to monke  
  - Get elected mayor  
  - Get sacrificed by a cult  
  - Get abducted by aliens

It’d be interesting but difficult to have a storyline where you get sucked back in time to a previous point in the game. It’d be fairly easy to handle just going to a previous turn. A multiple timeline approach. But if you tried to do a single timeline, where you see yourself doing stuff during the game, and then later events transpire so that, no matter what, you end up doing those things, that’d be kind of interesting. 

It’d also be interesting if there was a quest line where you time travel, and have the choice of preserving time travel (by doing what you were shown to do before) or breaking time travel (doing something different) with different quest outcomes

# Skill Checks Brainstorm

### Lights over the Town

Lights are seen over the town. It will turn out to be aliens that want to jam.

Taking the case gives you:

- Research the archives for similar sightings (**knowledge**)  
- Interview eye witnesses (**interpersonal**)  
- Set up an observation station (**focus**)

So you research the archives. You find similar sightings recorded during ancient times. The sky gods creating the lights would bestow gifts on those who played certain music.

You interview eye witnesses. The marching band  says they appear whenever they’re trying to practice, but the lights make their own noise which screws up their tests.

The observation station observes the lights, and also detects a series of faint sounds. The lights appear to arrive when loud music is played in the town.

After any of the three checks are passed, the investigators can try and set up contact. Sound appears to be important so they need some audio to attract the lights.

They can trick the local marching band to help, or just pay them. (**interpersonal or money**)  
\[if passed interpersonal check\] They can rent sound amplifying equipment (or “borrow” it from the music festival (**Sly or money**)  
\[if passed knowledge check\] They can carry the equipment up the mountains where the rock formations naturally amplify sounds (**resilience check**)

The concert with the lights in the sky commences. The player directs the band to jam with the lights in the sky. If they fail the check, the lights in the sky seemingly mimic the bad playing of the band, and everyone is humiliated. If they play very well, the lights in the sky reveal themselves to be an alien spaceship. CASE SOLVED

The aliens then try to beam up one of the investigators. The investigator can agree to be beamed up. They will later return with cosmic knowledge. The investigators can alternatively offer up one of the band geeks who seems desperate to go. “Thank goodness for permission slips.”

### Concerned Parents

Parents are concerned the kids at school are behaving weirdly. It’ll turn out that the kids are sending their eyes to a streamer.

“Interview parents” (no check)

The kids are wearing weird masks as part of some online trend. The kids are more and more insistent on always keeping their masks on.

“Interview kids” (hard interpersonal check)  
If passed, one kid mentions the name of an online streamer, before being angrily shushed by the other kids.  
If failed, you feel like the kids are delighted to keep their secret  
“Monitor kids” (sly check)   
If failed people think you’re a creep and future checks in the case are harder  
If passed, you see all the masked kids obsessively watching the same streamer  
“Take a kid’s mask” (no check)    
	The kid without the mask keeps glancing nervously at one of the other masked kids  
“Take that kid’s mask” (violence check)  
	If passed, after fighting the kids, you reveal that under that kid’s mask has a bandaged eye. Pulling the bandage back reveals the eye is missing.   
“Drag kid to his parents” (easy resilience check)  
	If passed, the kid admits to his parents that he removed his own eye and sent it to an online streamer. The other kids are planning to do this as well.

*Should there be a beat here where it’s shown a lot of kids have removed their eyes, or are planning on removing their eyes?*

“Investigate the stream” (focus \+ otherness check)  
	If failed, it just seems like a regular streamer. Hundreds of hours of a masked streamer playing boring videogames for kids  
If passed, the stream is interspersed with subliminal message urging the audience to give their eyes to the stream. It seems intended to encourage “views,” but the subliminal message is badly translated from another language. 

“Report streamer” (no check)  
	Someone will probably check the report eventually. CASE PARTIALLY SOLVED

*Feel like there should be a Dealing with The Eye Thief case following this, which the player can opt into.* 

### Voices

Voices are heard in the woods. It will turn out that the birds all have microphones in them for some reason, and a technical issue is causing the microphones to emit sound

Taking the case results in:  
“Interview Witnesses” (**easy interpersonal check**)  
	Success: Many campers agree they’ve heard the voices, faintly and coming from different directions in the woods. They don’t seem to be saying anything sinister though. More like idle small-talk  
	Failure: Many campers agree they’ve heard the voices, faintly and coming from different directions in the woods. The witnesses are vague and contradictory about the nature of the voice’s message.  
“Listen for voices” (**easy focus check**)  
	Success: You hear the voices, though they are faint. The voices seem to be discussing… the weather, and plans for the weekend. One voice idly complains about the local sport team’s recent performance?  
	Failure: You hear the voices, but the sound is too faint. You can’t make out what they are saying.  
“Locate the source of the voices” (**hard focus check**)  
	Success: You realize the voices are emanating from the small random birds flying about the area.   
	Failure: You will need more time in the woods  
“Spend more time in the woods” (**easy resilience check**)  
	Success: back to previous step  
	Failure: You get frustrated and go back to town  
“Catch one of the ‘talking’ birds” (**Sly or Violence**)  
	Success: You find strange electronics fused to the physiology of the bird\!  
	Failure: They keep getting away\! (can try again with some penalty?)  
“Listen to the voices clearly”  
	You hear two voices complaining about an unknown third party. The complaints are petty and regard “scheduling meetings that could have been emails.”  
“Investigate the microphone yourself” (**knowledge check**)  
“Take the bird with the microphone to an AV expert” (**costs money**)  
	Success: The bird seems to be bioengineered to contain surveillance equipment. However, mutations in the bird’s physique have reversed the attached microphone, turning it into a speaker instead. Whoever is trying to record you is accidentally broadcasting their own conversation.  
“Report your findings” (no check)  
You hear “They’re on to us.” emit from the bird. All other birds in the area abruptly fly away in different directions. CASE SOLVED

### Mutilated remains

Animal remains are found strangely mutilated. The concept is that a cult wants to bring back Egyptian embalming and is practicing on animals

“Take the case”   
	A large pile of strangely mutilated animals have been found in the woods.   
“Organize and analyse the corpse pile” (easy resilience \+ focus check)  
	Success: The investigators organize the corpses. The animals are mostly common pets. Many dogs and cats, plus the occasional bird, ferret, snake, or mouse. Although left outside, the corpses are strangely not rotting as much as one would expect.  
	Failure: The investigator isn’t too jazzed about digging through a pile of mutilated corpses and kind of slacks off. (Wastes a day. Can repeat with no check)  
“Analyse the nature of the mutilation” (easy focus check)  
	Success: The internal organs of each animal have been removed. The brain appears to have been removed through an incision on the face under the nose. The corpses have been dried out to reduce decay.  
	Failure: Something is definitely off here, but the investigators can’t put their finger on what. (Wastes a day. Can repeat with no check)  
“Brainstorm explanations” (otherness \+ knowledge)  
	Success:  The mutilation is consistent with the ritual of Egyptian mummification, but incomplete and applied to random household animals.   
	Failure: You can think of no explanation for this strangeness, but the animals look like they could have been former pets.  
“Check the corpses for pet tracking chips” (focus check)  
	Success: You find several pet tracking chips amongst the corpses and get the contact information of their owners.  
	Failure: You understand the task but have no idea how any of this works. You’ll have to pay a vet for help.  
“Pay a vet for help” (costs money)  
	The vet finds several pet tracking chips amongst the corpses and gives you the contact information of the owners  
“Contact owners” (if you failed to find the mummification, interpersonal check)  
Success: The pet owners are irate. They all seem to have paid for their deceased pets to receive ancient Egyptian burial rites and then be entombed in a small pyramid. They demand to know why their pet’s corpse was found in a pile in the woods.  
“Confront Egyptian pet mummification service”  
No check: You come across a woman in overalls crying with a defeated expression surrounded by piles of bricks and half finished pyramids.  
“Oh no. You found the unfinished product\! I’m sorry. I just didn’t know my service would be so popular” she blubbers. “Every pet will get their pyramid. I just didn’t know how much to charge people and I low-balled myself. Oh god, I’m so in over my head. Please don’t tell my customers. You have no idea how hard it is to pay off a history degree.” CASE SOLVED

### Graveyard activity	

	Something strange is going on in the graveyard. It’ll turn out that the tombstones are shit-talking the living. 

“Investigate the graveyard”  
	A group of angry mourners are gathered for a funeral. Most are furious. Some are crying. A few are laughing. Everyone seems to be responding to the gravestones.  
“Investigate a gravestone”  
	The epitate on the gravestone reads “Eat shit.” A few moments later, the words on the gravestone somehow shift. The gravestone now reads “Suck my balls.”  
“Talk to mourners” (interpersonal check)  
	Success: The gravestone now reads “Go blow it out your ass.” The mourners say the funeral is for a sweet old grandmother who would never talk like this. One of the mourners in the back seems skeptical, but doesn’t want to say what she’s thinking.  
	Failure: The gravestone now reads “Go blow it out your ass.” The mourners say the funeral is for a sweet old grandmother who would never talk like this  
“Talk to the skeptical mourner alone” (sly \+ interpersonal)  
	Success: The investigators manage to get the skeptical mourner away from the rest of the family. Once alone, she says the dead grandma was indeed very sweet, but her family chunked her in a nursing home and forgot about her. She tried to maintain her dignity till the end, but underneath it all she was really mad.  
	Failure: The skeptical mourner doesn’t want to speak ill of the dead   
“Study the grave” (otherness check \+ focus)  
	Success: The  gravestone now reads “Choke on a bag of dicks.” All sensors indicate an acute case of haunting, with an angry poltergeist changing the carving on the gravestone  
“Commune with the spirit of the dead” (if you have a medium)  
“Hire a medium to commune with the spirit of the dead” (costs money)  
	Success: The ghost keeps slinging insults (with the gravestone now reading “Go fuck a cactus”), But between insults, the ghost implies she’ll calm down if they dig up her corpse and her family apologize to it personally  
“Get the family to agree to apologize to the ghost’s dug-up corpse” (interpersonal)  
	Success: The gravestone now reads “Drown in piss.” The family agrees to whatever the ghost demands to calm the angry spirit  
	Failure: The family insists they’ve done nothing wrong  
“Exhume the coffin” (resolve)  
	Success or failure: The investigators exhume the coffin while the family of the deceased gather to apologize. However, when the coffin is opened, there’s no corpse inside. Instead, there’s just a giant pile of shit, which explodes and covers the gathered mourners in filth. The cackling of the old dead woman can be heard on the wind, as her spirit seems to have now found peace. CASE CLOSED

### Shared dreams

	Citizens report they had the same dream. Taking the case reveals  
“Interview witnesses” (interpersonal check)  
	Success: A group of people all recall seeing the same strange thing in their dreams. In the dream, they’re on a red planet before a strange, purple temple-like structure.  
“Probe the dreamers for more information” (sly \+ otherness check)  
	Success: Some dreamers remember better than others, but all are hazy on the details. You’ll need to find an especially lucid dreamer.  
Failure: The investigators make no progress.    
“Find out if more people had the same dream” (resolve check)  
	Success: The investigators listen to random people tediously talk about their dreams for hours and hours. It’s miserable, but they find others who have seen the strange temple. One dreamer is especially adapt at recalling vivid details  
“Aid the dreamer by building a sensory deprivation chamber” (sly \+ focus)  
	Success: The lucid dreamer can now describe the strange temple as if they were travelling there while awake  
	Failure: The attempts at helping the dreamer with a sensory deprivation chamber are unsuccessful. But they may still be able to recall the dream clearly enough to solve the case  
“Solve the case of the shared dream” (otherness \+ knowledge)  
	Success: The dreamer describes the stars in the sky above the temple in such detail, that the investigators can approximate its location in the galaxy, many thousands of lightyears away. Deciphering the inscription on the “temple” reveals it is a broadcasting device, that was built long ago to find other life in the universe. The project was deemed a failure and abandoned by its creators. CASE SOLVED

# Investigator Stats:

* Exploitability  
  * The investigator’s willingness to do whatever you want them to do. Highly exploitable investigators never quit, and will work without pay.  
* Focus  
  * The investigator’s ability to concentrate and crunch their way through a problem, especially if its boring or repetitive.   
* Interpersonal  
  * The investigator’s ability to communicate with people, empathize, anticipate human behavior, or build rapport.   
* Violence  
  * The investigator’s ability to do physical harm, or get the better of enemies attempting violence against them.  
* Sly  
  * The investigator’s ability to deceive, sneak, trick, or outwit  
* Knowledge  
  * The investigator’s ability to research or recall information. Knowledgeable investigators may be able to scour libraries for information, or they may already know the information in question before the case even begins  
* Resilience  
  * The investigator’s ability to tough it out, whatever it is. Whether its pain, boredom, fear, or otherwise, a resilient investigator keeps calm and carries on.  
* Otherness  
  * The investigators affinity for paranormality. Investigators with high otherness are comfortable communing with spirits, navigating alien architectures, or sensing cosmic energies
